deviations.what: t4's fourth criterion says a rule whose max_mib is under min_victim_mib renders as blamed-never-killed. The page instead says 'under 2.0 GiB (min_victim_mib) a match is blamed, never killed', because the guard compares each process's anonymous memory with min_victim_mib (memkill.py:255), not the rule's max_mib; a process over such a rule is killable once it passes min_victim_mib.
deviations.reason: the plan text came from docs/contracts/memory.md:117-118, which states the rule loosely; the code is the authority

deviations.what: an apply that reaches the box writes two audit lines (an attempt line before the call, the outcome after it), not one; a version-gate refusal writes one
deviations.reason: the audit line must exist before a write is sent, so a failed audit can refuse the write; the outcome is only known afterwards
